english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab:

That ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz delayed the prayer one day. ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr came in to him and informed him that al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah had delayed the prayer one day while he was in Iraq. Abu Mas‘ud al-Ansari came in to him and said: “What is this, Mughirah? Did you not know that Jibril, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, descended and prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed? Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he said: ‘This is what I was commanded to do.’” ‘Umar said to ‘Urwah: “Know what you are relating. Was it indeed Jibril who established the time of prayer for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?”
‘Urwah said: That is how Bashir ibn Abi Mas‘ud used to relate it from his father. ‘Urwah said: And ‘A’ishah related to me:
That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sunlight was in her chamber, before it rose out of it.

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: Shaqiq related to me. He said: I heard Hudhayfah say:

We were sitting with ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said: “Which of you remembers the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about tribulation?” I said: “I do, as he said it.” He said: “You are certainly bold about him—or about it.” I said: “A man’s trial in his family, his wealth, his child and his neighbour is expiated by prayer, fasting, charity, commanding and forbidding.” He said: “This is not what I mean, but the tribulation that surges as the sea surges.” He said: “You have nothing to fear from it, Commander of the Believers. Between you and it is a closed door.” He said: “Will it be broken or opened?” He said: “It will be broken.” He said: “Then it will never be closed.”

We said: “Did ‘Umar know the door?” He said: “Yes, just as tonight comes before tomorrow. I related to him a report containing no misleading statements.” We were afraid to ask Hudhayfah, so we told Masruq to do so. He asked him, and he said: “The door is ‘Umar.”

It is the most intense heat that you experience and the most intense bitter cold that you experience.”

arabic_blocks: [545] حدثنا محمود قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرني ابن جريج قال: أخبرني نافع قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ شغل عنها ليلة فأخرها حتى رقدنا في المسجد ثم استيقظنا ثم رقدنا ثم استيقظنا ثم خرج علينا النبي ﷺ، ثم قال ليس أحد من أهل الأرض ينتظر الصلاة غيركم وكان ابن عمر لا يبالي أقدمها أم أخرها إذا كان لا يخشى أن يغلبه النوم عن وقتها وكان يرقد قبلها قال ابن جريج قلت لعطاء، فقال: سمعت ابن عباس يقول أعتم رسول الله ﷺ ليلة بالعشاء حتى رقد الناس واستيقظوا ورقدوا واستيقظوا فقام عمر بن الخطاب، فقال الصلاة قال عطاء قال ابن عباس فخرج نبي الله ﷺ كأني أنظر إليه الآن يقطر رأسه ماء واضعا يده على رأسه، فقال لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم أن يصلوها هكذا فاستثبت عطاء كيف وضع النبي ﷺ على رأسه يده كما أنبأه بن عباس فبدد لي عطاء بين أصابعه شيئا من تبديد ثم وضع أطراف أصابعه على قرن الرأس ثم ضمها يمرها كذلك على الرأس حتى مست إبهامه طرف الأذن مما يلي الوجه على الصدغ وناحية اللحية لا يقصر ولا يبطش إلا كذلك، وقال لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم أن يصلوا هكذا
english_blocks: Mahmud related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed me. He said: Nafi‘ informed me. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to us:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was occupied one night and delayed it until we fell asleep in the mosque, then awoke, then fell asleep, then awoke. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and said: “No one on earth is waiting for the prayer except you.”
Ibn ‘Umar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, provided he did not fear that sleep would overcome him and cause him to miss its time. He used to sleep before it.
Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ‘Ata’, and he said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ one night until the people fell asleep and awoke, and fell asleep and awoke. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: “The prayer!” ‘Ata’ said: Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out—as though I were looking at him now—with water dripping from his head and his hand resting on it. He said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray it like this.”

I asked ‘Ata’ to confirm how the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ‘Abbas had informed him. ‘Ata’ spread his fingers apart a little for me, then placed his fingertips on the side of his head. Then he brought them together, drawing them across his head like that until his thumb touched the edge of his ear next to his face, at the temple and towards the beard, neither slowing down nor hurrying, but just like that. And he said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray like this.”
